newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Main southeast Albanian town falls to rebels.
newsitem.headline: Main southeast Albanian town falls to rebels.

text.p: Korce, the main town in southeast Albania, fell to rebels on Thursday, leaving the southern half of the Balkan country almost entirely in the hands of anti-government forces, witnesses said.
Greek television showed jubilant rebels racing captured tanks and armoured personnel carriers through central Korce, close to the Greek border.

Witnesses said several people had been wounded in shooting during the seizure of Korce. But it was unclear whether this was from wild shooting during celebrations, or from exchanges of fire with security forces.

Greek television showed men and boys looting an army weapons depot outside the town, and witnesses said guards had abandoned the border point at nearby Kapshtice, the second main crossing point into Greece.

Armed rebels opened the customs and passport stations and waved through cars and trucks. The main Albania-Greece crossing at Kakavia has been deserted since last week. Armed gangs have been extorting money from travellers at the border point.
Korce is one of the last major towns in southern Albania to fall to the rebels, who launched a popular uprising against the government of President Sali Berisha 10 days ago.
Its fall means the rebels control almost the entire south of the Balkan country of 3.4 million people. The rebels want Berisha to resign and new general elections to be held.
Greek television showed men and boys at the Korce army munitions depot gleefully ripping open crates of assault rifles, grenades and other weapons. Trucks arrived to load up on looted weapons.
About six boys, who appeared to be below 13 years old, stood on an abandoned tank and one fired his newly seized Kalashnikov rifles in the air while the others winced.
A group of about 20 close-cropped young conscripts walked away from the scene unarmed.
"The officers ran away first, then we followed," one soldier said. "We had nothing to eat but onions and cabbage".
The conscripts said they would walk to their homes.
Greece has increased security along its long border with Albania, fearing a wave of refugees as violence sweeps the country. Greece already has some 350,000 illegal Albanians.
